_meta.schema: Quarter-keyed analyst briefings for the System Monitor tab. Keys are 'YYYY-MM-DD' for the last day of the quarter; values are 4-6 sentence prose paragraphs in the style specified by briefing.jsx. Bank tickers in the prose (UNIBK, SOGEBK, BNC, etc.) are auto-linkified by the BriefingText component.
_meta.voice: Dry, factual, observational. No generic framing, no threshold restatement, no hedging. Lead with the most material developments; close with one watch-item if relevant.
_meta.next_steps: When Q2 2026 data lands (likely Sep-Oct 2026), add a '2026-06-30' key with a fresh briefing. Eventually this file may be regenerated by a Python script that calls the Anthropic API server-side.

2025-12-31: The quarter closed on a contradictory note: total assets and deposits accelerated (+8.8% and +9.2% YoY respectively) while gross loans contracted -2.3% YoY, pushing system Liq/Deposits to 69.3% — an extraordinary buffer that reflects continued credit retrenchment rather than a deposit shock. UNIBK (NPL 0.45%, CAR 28.5%, gross loans +6.2% YoY) remained the only large bank growing its book and continues to look untroubled, while SOGEBK pulled back further (gross loans -7.6% YoY) with NPL drifting up to 5.70% (+87 bp QoQ) and Cap/Assets the thinnest among the large banks at 6.34%. BNC's headline NPL improved sharply to 39.81% (-8.7 pp QoQ) and provision coverage rose to 0.65× (+10 pp YoY), but most of the ratio improvement reflects an -11.8% YoY contraction in the loan book rather than recoveries — denominator effect, not asset-quality cure. CAPITALBK posted a striking ROE jump to 21.2% (+11.2 pp YoY) on +7.4% YoY gross loan growth, though its provision coverage collapsed to 0.02× from roughly 1.2× a year earlier — anomalous and worth watching even off a small base. System CAR climbed to 26.2% (+3.2 pp QoQ) and provision coverage just crossed 1.0× for the first time in the recent series; profitability (system ROE 15.4%, +3.8 pp YoY) is the strongest in years. Watch-item: with system loans still shrinking in nominal HTG and inflation running near 30%, the real-credit picture is materially worse than the headline ratios suggest — the system is delivering its strongest profitability while quietly disintermediating the real economy.
2026-03-31: Q1 2026 confirmed the credit-retreat-with-profitability paradox of late 2025: system gross loans contracted a further -1.5% YoY (moderating from -2.3% in Q4) while deposits grew +10.2% YoY, leaving Liq/Deposits at 70.5% and lifting system ROE to a multi-year high of 16.0% (+3.1 pp YoY). The most notable bank-level move was UNIBK's NPL ticking up to 1.10% (+65 bp QoQ from 0.45%) — still negligible in absolute terms but the first asset-quality wobble at the system's largest book in some time, alongside a -4.7% QoQ loan pullback that breaks UNIBK's 'only large bank still lending' posture from recent quarters. SOGEBK's NPL stabilized at 5.62% (-7 bp QoQ) without further book shrinkage, and BNC's headline NPL held at 39.66% (-15 bp QoQ) with loans even ticking up +0.6% QoQ — the Q4 improvement is not reversing, though loans remain -8.9% YoY so the ratio is still held down by denominator effects rather than recoveries. BPH presents the most extreme picture: gross loans collapsed -62.8% QoQ to HTG 0.5 bn and NPL jumped to 75.3%, with the reported CAR spiking to an essentially-meaningless 135% as RWA evaporated alongside the loan book — a near-orderly wind-down. BUH was the lone bright spot for credit, growing gross loans +8.2% QoQ and +5.2% YoY, the strongest of any reporting bank, while CAPITALBK's previously-flagged near-zero provision coverage (0.04× vs ~1.2× a year ago) is still not recovering despite continued profitability (ROE 19.4%, +7.7 pp YoY). Watch-item: CPI inflation was 20.6% YoY in March 2026 (and accelerated to 21.0% in April), so the headline 16.0% system ROE is still roughly -4 pp in real terms — the strong nominal numbers continue to mask real-economy disintermediation as nominal-HTG loan books shrink against double-digit inflation.
